subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` immediately fail closed for every legacy ownerless session row, or must an ownership migration or recovery path ship first?
rationale: The strict rule matches the established delete boundary, but it intentionally stops previously permitted mutations of persisted ownerless rows and therefore needs explicit ownership of the security-versus-upgrade tradeoff.

options.title: Fail Closed Now
options.body: Keep strict owner equality and document or prove that operators and non-plugin clients can recover legacy ownerless sessions.

options.title: Migrate Legacy Rows
options.body: Add a bounded doctor or ownership migration before enforcing strict plugin-runtime patch authorization on existing rows.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed Now
recommendation.body: Keep strict owner equality and document or prove that operators and non-plugin clients can recover legacy ownerless sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The current projection and lifecycle implementation history makes this the strongest available owner for the security and upgrade choice.
